source.title: Lurgan Mail, 10 May 1902, p. 5 ("Lurgan Rural": "the following have been elected unopposed")
source.publisher: Lurgan Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name read from the page image; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the rural district council (ten Co. Armagh divisions, two councillors each), 1902: every division returned unopposed. No party labels are printed. Returned unopposed. James Campbell: no party label printed in 1902. At other elections he stood as Nationalist (Montiaghs, 27 May 1908, listed as Nationalist: Irish Weekly and Ulster Examiner, 6 June 1908, p. 9 ("Lurgan Rural District"); nominations from the Lurgan Mail, 2 May 1908, p. 4 ("Lurgan Rural Council": nominations)). The name stands at elections from 1899 to 1939 and may be a father and son.
